capture.final_message:
Use flatness as preservation of injective maps under tensor product.

For the first conjunct, tensor the injective map \(f:R\to M\) with \(N\). Flatness of \(N\) makes
\[
f\otimes \mathrm{id}_N:R\otimes_R N\longrightarrow M\otimes_R N
\]
injective. Since \(R\otimes_R N\simeq N\) and \(N\) is nontrivial, the target must also be nontrivial.

For the second conjunct:

1. Express linear independence of \((w_j)_{j\in t}\) as injectivity of the linear-combination map
   \[
   R^{(t)}\longrightarrow N.
   \]
2. Tensor this map with \(M\). Flatness of \(M\) preserves its injectivity.
3. Identify
   \[
   M\otimes_R R^{(t)}\simeq M^{(t)}.
   \]
   Under this identification, \(v_i\otimes w_j\) is represented before the injective map by the finitely supported family having \(v_i\) in coordinate \(j\).
4. A finite relation among these coordinate vectors splits coordinatewise in \(j\); each resulting relation among the \(v_i\) vanishes by the independence of \(v\) on \(s\).

Thus the product-indexed tensor family is linearly independent on \(s\times t\). The essential assumptions are precisely the relevant flatness hypotheses, which ensure that the injective linear-combination maps remain injective after tensoring.
